technique_why: A soft blended background with a few big shapes in front of it suits back-to-front painting, and the chickadee is built from simple pieces and marks a beginner can make.
subject: A black-capped chickadee perched on a curved brown branch in autumn, with red and gold leaves hanging nearby and a low sun glowing through hazy orange woods
focal_point: The chickadee's black cap, white cheek and dark eye, just left of the sun
light: From the low sun at the upper right, behind and to the right of the bird: lit edges face up and to the right, shadows fall on the lower left of every form
why: We start with the whole background blended wet in one go, then the sun, the hazy far trunks and the soft autumn dabs, so everything behind is done before anything sharp goes on. Then the branch and the hanging leaves are blocked in and given their dark and light, and most of the lesson goes to the chickadee: its shape, its pale patches, its black and gray markings, its feathers, and the face last, so the focal point gets the most care.

things.name: The blue and gold sky
things.why: The whole background is a soft blend from blue to gold, laid wet in one go behind everything.
things.called: the smooth blue and gold background color

things.name: The low sun
things.why: A small pale disk with a soft glow, painted in small circles in one move.

things.name: The hazy far trunks
things.why: Far trunks in a wood, pulled once in a soft blue-gray with no bark detail because they are far away.

things.name: The far autumn leaves
things.why: Hazy autumn woods: soft dabbed patches, dark first then lighter, with no sharp leaf shapes.
things.called: the soft orange and red-orange patches in the background

things.name: The trunk and curved branch
things.why: The trunk and the thick arching perch are one solid shape a teacher builds from bands, then shades below and lights on top, with the twigs added last by liner; trunks-branches has no shading step for wood this close.
things.plain: the plain mid-brown trunk and branch shape

things.name: The hanging leaves
things.why: Each big leaf is a shaped object built from a teardrop and lobes, then shaded, lit, and given its stem and veins.
things.plain: four flat leaf shapes, two golden yellow and two red-orange

things.name: The chickadee
things.why: The closest fit: the bird is built as a shape, shaded, given pale patches and its black and gray markings, feathered with flicks, and the face last. It lacks only that it is written for fur; the flicks here are feathers, lying down and back from the head.
things.plain: the plain warm buff bird shape
things.left_out: The fine barbs of each wing and tail feather and the thin white feather edges; the wing and tail are suggested with a few dark lines and light flicks.

things.name: The legs and feet
things.why: Thin dark legs and toes gripping the branch, a few liner lines over dry paint.

steps.name: Blend the blue and gold sky

lays.what: the whole canvas: soft blue at the left, the top left and along the bottom, warming to golden orange across the middle and up the right, and pale yellow in the upper right where the sun will be

steps.after: The whole canvas is a soft criss-cross blend: blue on the left, at the top left and along the bottom, golden orange across the middle and right, pale yellow in the upper right. There is no sun disk, no trees, leaves, branch or bird yet.
steps.why: Everything else sits on this, so it goes on first and right past where the branch and bird will be.

steps.name: Circle in the sun

lays.what: a round pale cream disk in the upper right, with a ring of pale yellow circles around it fading into the gold

steps.after: A soft pale cream sun glows in the upper right, ringed by pale yellow that melts into the golden sky. The rest of the canvas is still the plain blended sky.

steps.name: Pull the hazy far trunks

lays.what: two tall soft blue-gray trunks in the right third running top to bottom, a few thinner fainter ones beside them, and faint trunk shapes low at the left and bottom middle

steps.after: Soft hazy blue-gray trunks stand in the right third and faintly at the lower left and bottom, with soft edges and no bark. The sky and sun show everywhere else.

steps.name: Dab the red-orange far leaves

lays.what: loose patches of red-orange dabs scattered across the background: down the left side, across the middle, around the far trunks at the right and along the bottom, with sky showing between

steps.after: Soft red-orange dabbed patches are scattered over the background on the left, middle, right and bottom, with blue and gold sky between them. No lighter orange on them yet.

steps.name: Dab the light orange over the far leaves

lays.what: lighter orange dabs over most of each patch, more on the upper and right sides facing the sun, leaving red-orange showing underneath

steps.after: The far leaf patches are soft orange with red-orange still showing at their lower edges, like hazy autumn woods. The background is finished; the canvas has no branch, leaves or bird yet.

steps.name: Block in the trunk and branch

lays.what: the whole trunk and branch as one flat mid-brown shape: first the trunk as a long band up the left edge, then the thick branch arching from its base across to the right and thinning to a point, then the thin side branch at the top left

steps.after: A flat mid-brown trunk rises up the left side, and a flat brown branch arches from its base across the canvas to the lower right, with a thin side branch at the top left. No shading, light, twigs or leaves yet.

steps.name: Block in the hanging leaves

lays.what: four flat leaves, each a center teardrop with a pointed lobe on each side: a golden yellow leaf and a red-orange leaf at the top left, a golden yellow and a red-orange leaf hanging below the branch at the right

steps.after: Four flat leaf shapes hang in place, two golden yellow and two red-orange, with no stems, veins, shading or light. The branch is still plain flat brown.

steps.name: Shade the leaves
steps.unit: The branch and leaves' shading and light

lays.what: deep gold along the center and the shaded left side of each gold leaf, deep red along the center and the shaded left side of each red leaf

steps.after: Each leaf has a darker side and center, deep gold on the gold leaves and deep red on the red ones, with its main color still showing on the right. No light edges, stems or veins yet.

steps.name: Light the leaves' sunny edges

lays.what: light gold on the upper right edges and tips of the gold leaves, coral orange on the upper right edges of the red leaves

steps.after: The leaves have a dark side, a middle, and a light edge facing the sun. They still have no stems or veins.

steps.name: Shade the trunk and branch

lays.what: dark brown along the underside of the branch and down the left side of the trunk, in broken bark patches

steps.after: The branch and trunk are dark brown underneath and on the left in broken patches, mid brown on top. No light on top and no twigs yet.

steps.name: Catch the sun on the branch

lays.what: warm tan along the top of the branch, brightest where it arches under the bird, and down the right side of the trunk

steps.after: The top of the branch and the right side of the trunk catch warm tan light, over mid brown, over dark brown below. The thin twigs at the branch's end are not there yet.

steps.name: Line the twigs, stems and veins

lays.what: the thin twigs forking off the right end of the branch, tapering to points
each leaf's thin stem curving up to the branch, and a center vein with a few side veins in each leaf

steps.after: Thin dark twigs fork off the right end of the branch, and each leaf hangs from the wood on a thin stem with a dark center vein and side veins. The branch and leaves are finished; the bird is not painted yet.
steps.why: One move: the same liner and the same thinned dark brown, done in one pass while it is loaded.

steps.name: Block in the chickadee

lays.what: the whole bird as one flat warm buff shape: a big oval body on the branch first, then a round head at its upper right, then the long tail as a tapering wedge out to the lower left

steps.after: A flat warm buff bird shape sits on the branch: round body, round head, long tail to the left. No shading, cap, cheek, wing, eye, beak or legs yet.

steps.name: Shade the bird's underside

lays.what: buff shadow curved along the lower belly, the left flank and under the head, leaving warm buff on the lit right side

steps.after: The buff bird is darker along its belly, left side and under the head, lighter on the right. Still no cap, cheek, wing or face.

steps.name: Paint the white cheek and chest

lays.what: a creamy white cheek patch across the side of the head and the white front of the chest under it, in 2 to 3 thin coats

steps.after: The head has a creamy white cheek and the front of the chest is creamy white, fading into the buff belly. The cap, bib and wing are not painted yet.

steps.name: Paint the black cap and bib

lays.what: the black cap over the top of the head down to the eye line, and the black bib under the beak down the throat, leaving the white cheek between them

steps.after: The head has a black cap and a black bib with the white cheek between them. No eye or beak yet, and the wing is still buff.

steps.name: Paint the gray wing and tail

lays.what: the gray wing curving along the bird's back from below the cap to the tail, and the long gray tail out to the lower left

steps.after: A smooth blue-gray wing lies along the back and the gray tail points to the lower left, with no feather lines yet.

steps.name: Pull the dark wing feather lines

lays.what: a few dark tapering lines along the wing and tail where the long feathers overlap, following their direction down and back

steps.after: The wing and tail show a few dark feather lines on the gray. The belly and chest have no feather flicks yet.

steps.name: Flick the belly feathers

lays.what: short light buff flicks over the belly and flank, lying down and back from the head, leaving the darker buff showing between them

steps.after: The buff belly looks soft and feathery with darker buff between the flicks. The wing is still plain gray with dark lines, and there is no face.

steps.name: Flick light into the wing and tail

lays.what: light gray flicks along the edges of the wing feathers and down the tail, leaving the dark lines showing

steps.after: The wing and tail have light gray feather edges beside the dark lines. The chest's sunlit edge is not brightened yet.

steps.name: Flick the sunlit edge of the chest

lays.what: a few creamy white flicks only on the right edge of the chest and cheek, facing the sun

steps.after: The bird's right edge glows creamy white where the sun catches it. There is still no eye, beak or legs.

steps.name: Paint the eye and beak

lays.what: a small round black eye where the cap meets the white cheek, and a short pointed black beak at the front of the head

steps.after: The bird has a round dark eye at the edge of its cap and a short pointed beak. No shine in the eye and no legs yet.

steps.name: Line the legs and feet

lays.what: two thin dark legs from the belly down to the branch, and the curled toes gripping over the top of the branch

steps.after: Two thin dark legs come down from the belly and the toes curl over the branch. Only the eye shine is missing.

steps.name: Dot the light in the eye

lays.what: one tiny creamy white catch light in the upper right of the eye

steps.after: The finished painting: the eye shines with a tiny light, and the chickadee sits on its sunlit branch among the hanging leaves and the glowing autumn woods.
